outcome: rejected: the cold TP3 launch loaded the native target and draft weights, then exhausted unified-memory headroom while compiling the selected DeepSeek V4.1 indexer JIT keys; all three hosts recovered by reboot and the candidate was not promoted
service_scope: only the three ranks of the single TP3 inference service were started; no Strix, auxiliary, reranking, scanner, or workload-worker container was running
last_completed_stages: all ranks formed NCCL 2.30.7 and selected RoCEnante for eligible TP collectives
all ranks selected B12X MXFP8 linear, MXFP4 MoE, and sparse-MLA paths
target plus DSpark loading reported 98.1 GiB per rank
all ranks prepared 226 B12X MXFP8 plans, 43 B12X MoE plans, and one RoCEnante plan before memory profiling

memory_observations.interpretation: the approximately 98.1 GiB model and 99.8 GiB container accounting do not include all driver, RDMA, host, compiler, and unified-memory residency; the Docker 112 GiB cgroup therefore did not preserve usable NVIDIA-driver headroom

jit_cache_evidence.result: patch 0022 selected model-owned kernels correctly, but their compilation still occurred after weight and plan residency

additional_gap: both selected disk-Engram query plans warned that they were prepared on first use rather than by the explicit startup preparation phase

recovery.post_recovery: all nodes reachable with approximately 116 GiB MemAvailable, zero swap use, and zero running containers

conclusion: do not promote patch 0022. Preserve its model/backend registration, but compile the 37 configuration-derived indexer keys in a GPU-backed, content-addressed cache-priming stage before loading weights. Separately account for retained B12X plans and register the selected Engram queries. A subsequent launch must prove zero cold indexer compilations and no driver allocation failures before quality or performance benchmarking.
